RC-01.name: Integration gap
RC-01.definition: Data exists in a source system but no pipe carries it to the consuming system.
RC-01.standard_remediation_pattern: Build the missing pipe; backfill common window with approval.

RC-02.name: Mapping error
RC-02.definition: A pipe exists but maps the wrong field, wrong granularity, or wrong semantic.
RC-02.standard_remediation_pattern: Fix mapping config; correct or era-flag affected records.

RC-03.name: Guest / anonymous identity
RC-03.definition: Commerce activity occurs without a durable identity the marketing platform can hold.
RC-03.standard_remediation_pattern: Email-first contact creation; capture-point improvements as workflow opportunities.

RC-04.name: Duplicate creation
RC-04.definition: Multiple entry points create parallel records for one real-world entity.
RC-04.standard_remediation_pattern: Merge plan with survivor designation; unify entry-point keys.

RC-05.name: Sync lag / timing
RC-05.definition: Pipes work but ordering, latency or scheduling produces stale or racing state.
RC-05.standard_remediation_pattern: Cadence contract + freshness SLA + heartbeat monitoring.

RC-06.name: Schema / definition drift
RC-06.definition: The meaning or shape of a field changed over time without migration.
RC-06.standard_remediation_pattern: Format contract per key; era boundaries flagged in canonical layer.

RC-07.name: Consent flow divergence
RC-07.definition: Consent capture, storage or propagation differs between systems.
RC-07.standard_remediation_pattern: Source-of-truth policy per direction; propagation loop wired.

RC-08.name: Manual entry / import artifact
RC-08.definition: Human-entered or bulk-imported data carrying format noise or junk.
RC-08.standard_remediation_pattern: Normalisation batches with approval; provenance cohort tagging.

RC-09.name: Historical migration gap
RC-09.definition: The integration started at a point in time; earlier truth was never loaded.
RC-09.standard_remediation_pattern: Approved backfill within the FD-05 window; declare residual blind spots.

RC-10.name: Deleted / archived residue
RC-10.definition: Entities removed in the source live on in downstream surfaces.

RC-11.name: Multi-store / multi-account ambiguity
RC-11.definition: Data from parallel stores, locales or sub-accounts mixed or mis-scoped.
RC-11.standard_remediation_pattern: Store/account registry (FD-06) enforced at every pipe.
RC-11.user_definition: More than one store or Manago account is in play, and Klints isn’t sure which data belongs where.

RC-12.name: Configuration error
RC-12.definition: Tracking code, feed config, scopes or platform settings wrong or absent.
RC-12.standard_remediation_pattern: Configuration audit + guided repair + verification test.

RC-13.name: API contract violation / type misuse
RC-13.definition: Integration uses the platform API outside its documented semantics.
RC-13.standard_remediation_pattern: Vocabulary contract; integration re-routing; never mutate types.

RC-14.name: Format / unit / timezone inconsistency
RC-14.definition: Same fact encoded differently: units, currency basis, TZ, date format.
RC-14.standard_remediation_pattern: Canonical normalisation rules; unit validation at ingestion.

RC-15.name: Volume loss
RC-15.definition: Records dropped by rate limits, retry expiry, or partial failures.
RC-15.standard_remediation_pattern: Ordering fixes, idempotent retries, gap-list recovery.
